newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lower turnout for France's annual anti-AIDS march.
newsitem.headline: Lower turnout for France's annual anti-AIDS march.

text.p: Thousands of people marched in French cities on Saturday to urge help for AIDS victims, but turnout was lower than in 1996 following medical progress against the deadly epidemic.
"Let's take a new step against AIDS," banners proclaimed in the fourth annual "March for Life" in France, the European nation hardest hit by Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome.

Organisers estimated that 10,000 people joined the colourful rally in Paris with dancers and music, half the number who took part in 1996. Smaller rallies were held in five other cities, partly timed to remind politicians of the disease on the eve of France's National Assembly election.
Marchers said promising new treatments and a decline in the number of deaths in France in 1996, for the first time since the start of the epidemic, may have cut turnout.

In February, the government said that 20,000 patients were being treated with the new class of drugs known as protease inhibitors. They work by preventing the AIDS virus from leaving a patient's DNA and invading the rest of the body.
France has 50,000 reported cases of the disease, 30,000 deaths and 110,000 people who have tested positive for the HIV virus that causes AIDS.
